problem.title: Running a company should not mean rebuilding the picture every morning.
problem.intro: Trenston started in management meetings. The decisions were often quick. Getting to them was the slow part.

items.title: The numbers live in different places
items.body: Money in one tool, pipeline in another, hiring in a third. Nobody has the whole picture, least of all the person responsible for it.

items.title: Status means asking
items.body: A big part of a leader's week goes into asking for updates and piecing the answers together from spreadsheets, email and chat.

items.title: Decisions get lost
items.body: Approvals vanish into chat threads. Weeks later, nobody can find what was decided, or why.

items.title: Missing data looks like zero
items.body: An empty cell can be mistaken for a zero, so a gap in the data quietly becomes a wrong number.

whyUs.title: Built around the person who has to decide.
whyUs.intro: Four things we chose to do differently.

items.title: It tells you what it does not know
items.body: Where data is missing, Trenston shows "Add data" instead of a made-up zero. Ask Trenston answers from your workspace and is instructed to say when something has not been entered.

items.title: It is built around the decision
items.body: The Decision Center ranks open calls, drafts a recommendation with a confidence score, and waits for you to confirm. Nothing becomes a decision until you do.

items.title: It sits on top of your tools
items.body: Connect QuickBooks, Xero, SAP Business One, HubSpot and Slack instead of replacing them. Start free and explore a built-in demo company before you enter anything.

items.title: It is a team workspace, not a solo dashboard
items.body: You hand work to managers and they work in it too. Each person sees their own departments, assignees get an email when work is delegated, and financial data stays limited to people you grant Financials access.
